text:
erin_sales: Prospect (EU payroll + benefits) dropped an RFP. they want a 14-day EU-only POC, a temporary SLA during the POC (they call it a 'bridge SLA'), KMS escrow proofs, and a signed sub-processor statement for procurement. they explicitly don't want to buy Dedicated yet. can we scope this without legal risk?
kai_se: short: Hosted can run a timeboxed EU-pref POC and we can produce artifacts. 'bridge SLA' is possible in a narrow scope but needs legal signoff and must be time-limited. we can't give contractual guarantees of absolute in-region processing in Hosted.
anita_ops: ops side: we can create a temporary policy that pins tenant -> eu-central-1 and disables cross-region fallback for the POC window. we'll enable netflow capture, connection traces (sanitized), and a KMS region audit for a scoped key. this is manual and requires a runbook and on-call approval.
erin_sales: procurement asked specifically: "Can you guarantee keys never leave the EU during the POC?"
leon_legal: answer: for the POC we can use a scoped regional key and provide KMS audit logs showing key usage region, but Hosted uses our managed multi-region key service by default. contractual guarantee "keys never leave EU" requires Dedicated/Private with BYOK/HSM. for the bridge SLA we can draft a time-limited addendum that describes the operational controls and remedies for breaches during the POC.
maya_finance: procurement will also ask for cost to add the bridge SLA and how that compares to full Dedicated. quick guidance: short POC bridge SLA + manual ops support = one-time professional service estimate (consulting/on-call) ~ $X-$Yk; Dedicated migration is multi-month with ongoing monthly commit (2-5x hosted unit cost ballpark). i'll model numbers after the POC scope.
kai_se: sample steer header to show the customer technical contact:```
POST /v1/chat/completions
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}
x-tenant-id: eu-payroll-poc
x-region-hint: eu-central-1
```
server side we will pin routing table entry for the tenant for the POC window.
anita_ops: deliverables we can provide at POC end: 1) netflow CSV for tenant flows, 2) sanitized connection trace mapping to regions, 3) KMS region audit CSV for the scoped key, 4) processing-path PNG, 5) sub-processor annex with flags for control-plane regions. note: some vendor control planes are multi-region; we will mark those and provide exported artifacts.
erin_sales: procurement also wants a signed sub-processor statement that we won't use US-based backups during the POC.
leon_legal: we can provide a scoped sub-processor statement for the POC window describing operational commitments (no cross-region backups for the tenant data in the POC), but it must be explicitly timeboxed and includes representations about provided artifacts only. cannot be open-ended.
anita_ops: timeline: need written customer approval of scope + test window. ops can schedule the manual pin in 3 business days after approval; we'll need a runbook review and on-call availability during the window.
maya_finance: i'll prep a pricing appendix for procurement: Hosted baseline, one-time bridge SLA fee (ops+on-call), optional regional reservation monthly estimate, Dedicated migration estimate.
erin_sales: good. can someone create the internal ticket and draft the bridge SLA language for procurement?
ops-bot: ticket RD-POC-1210 created, owners @anita_ops and @kai_se, action items: draft runbook, enable scoped KMS audit, prepare sub-processor annex. target kickoff in 3 business days.
leon_legal: i'll draft a 1-paragraph bridge SLA that covers scope, duration, monitoring, evidence to be shared, and remedies limited to POC window. will attach sub-processor annex template.
anita_ops: i'll list the exact monitoring signals we'll hand over: netflow CSV, KMS audit csv, region-tagged connection traces, routing table diff, and a processing path diagram.
erin_sales: perfect. i'll share the customer's RFP answers back here once i have them. thanks all :thumbsup:
